title: New ethionamide boosters and EthR2: structural and energetic analysis.
authors: Vianna, J F; Bezerra, K S; Lima Costa, A H; Barbosa, E D; Lima Neto, J X; Oliveira, J I N; Freire, V N; Fulco, U L
one_liner_zh: 该文通过晶体结构和DFT/MFCC计算分析EthR2转录抑制因子与抑制剂复合物的结合能，属于蛋白-小分子互作而非TF-DNA体系，但涉及转录因子结构建模与能量计算，方法可部分借鉴。
abstract: Ethionamide (ETH) is a high-profile drug for the treatment of patients with multidrug-resistant Mycobacterium tuberculosis and, in order to produce its inhibitory effects, it needs to be bioactivated by monooxygenase EthA. This process is under the control of the transcriptional repressors EthR and EthR2, so that their inhibition results in the boosting of ethionamide activation. Herein, through crystallographic data and computer simulations, we calculated the interaction binding energies of four inhibitors with improved in vitro potency, namely BDM76060 (PDB ID: 6HS1), BDM72201 (PDB ID: 6HRX), BDM76150 (PDB ID: 6HS2) and BDM72719 (PDB ID: 6HRY), in complexes with the transcriptional repressor EthR2, using density functional theory (DFT) within the molecular fractionation with conjugated caps (MFCC) approach. It was observed that these ligands share the same binding site within a 10.0 A radius of the EthR2 protein; however, their structural particularities have a significant impact on the global energies of systems. The BDM72201 and BDM72719 components are weakly attached to the binding site, while BDM76060 and BDM76150 components produce stronger bonds, corroborating with experimental studies demonstrating that BDM76060 and BDM76150 are more successful in producing inhibitory effects. BDM76060 and BDM76150 have many functional groups that increase the contact surface with the protein and attract a more significant number of amino acid residues, being able to produce polarities that generate stronger interactions. In the current scenario of a growing number of cases of bacterial resistance, the obtained data can be used to guide clinical trials of these inhibitors and other inhibitors that act on the alternative EthR2 pathway, focusing on improving the activity of ethionamide, its effectiveness, a reduction in the treatment time and exposure to cytotoxic effects.
abstract_zh: 乙硫异烟胺（Ethionamide, ETH）是一种备受关注的药物，用于治疗耐多药结核分枝杆菌（Mycobacterium tuberculosis）患者，为产生其抑制作用，需经单加氧酶EthA进行生物活化。此过程受转录抑制因子EthR和EthR2的调控，因此抑制这些因子可增强乙硫异烟胺的活化。本文中，通过晶体学数据和计算机模拟，我们利用密度泛函理论（density functional theory, DFT）结合分子片段化共轭帽（molecular fractionation with conjugated caps, MFCC）方法，计算了四种具有改善体外效力的抑制剂与转录抑制因子EthR2复合物中的相互作用结合能，即BDM76060（PDB ID: 6HS1）、BDM72201（PDB ID: 6HRX）、BDM76150（PDB ID: 6HS2）和BDM72719（PDB ID: 6HRY）。观察到这些配体在EthR2蛋白10.0 Å半径内共享同一结合位点；然而，其结构特性对系统的整体能量有显著影响。BDM72201和BDM72719组分与结合位点结合较弱，而BDM76060和BDM76150组分产生更强的键合，这与实验研究一致，表明BDM76060和BDM76150在产生抑制效果方面更为成功。BDM76060和BDM76150具有许多功能基团，增加了与蛋白的接触表面，并吸引更多数量的氨基酸残基，能够产生极性，从而形成更强的相互作用。在当前细菌耐药性病例日益增多的背景下，所获得的数据可用于指导这些抑制剂及其他作用于替代EthR2通路的抑制剂的临床试验，重点关注提高乙硫异烟胺的活性、其有效性、缩短治疗时间及减少细胞毒性暴露。
